publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The requirements to be fulfilled by an amplifier to be used for bio-electric research are discussed, and certain suitable circuits are described in outline, together with considerations relating to the limits of amplification obtainable in practice. articleTitle: The telephone and the laboratory — Part I
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The necessity for organized research resulted in the growth in America from about 1907 of the Bell Telephone Laboratories, with their present staff of 2 300 qualified engineers and scientists. In Great Britain the British Post Office has 300 such men engaged in research, their activities being largely co-ordinated with those of the manufacturing companies. The figure for Australia is 55. The Comité Consultatif International T él éphonique (Fernsprechen) (C.C.I.F.) and other bodies perform useful liaison functions. Outline financial data are given. In South Africa, with its comparatively small telephone system, most of the apparatus used has been imported. Work done has therefore consisted largely in the comparative quality testing of equipment and the investigation of problems arising from its use under South African conditions. With the growth of local industry the amount of material testing has increased. Investigations and development work have been carried out on telegraphs, radio, switching, long distance dialling, wires and dielectrics, and on telephone instruments. The high incidence of lightning has brought problems on underground cables, fusing and earthing. Research on lightning interference with V.F. telegraph systems is now in progress.

articleTitle: An investigation into pin corrosion on traction suspension insulators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The Aim of this paper is to examine the causes of insulator pm corrosion on d.c. insulators, and to this end experiments were conducted to determine the relative effect of different contaminations on leakage currents, in the presence of moist atmospheres. Further experiments were performed to explain the presence of brush discharge and to examine a few methods of alleviating pin corrosion. It was learned from these experiments that salt was the most important contaminating factor, soot a lesser factor and an acid film the least important factor. The average type of contamination acquired m service, containing neither visible salt nor soot, was of a nature intermediate between a pure salt and a pure soot film. It was thought that brush discharge occurred because of the contaminated condition of the underside of the insulator. With regard to preventive measures it was found that an insulating coat over the pin proved effective experimentally in reducing leakage current, but this has been found unsatisfactory in practice. Conversely a method found to be effective in operation, namely, that of surrounding the base of the pin with a lead washer, did not, under laboratory conditions, reduce leakage current. The conclusions reached were that load washers prevent corrosion by providing an alternative source of metal for electro-deposition; in addition the lead itself is inert to acid or atmospheric corrosion. It was thought that corrosion could be reduced by setting the pin in lead and by increasing the leakage distance of the upper portion of the insulator.

articleTitle: A review of British practice in the protection of electric power systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The protection of electric power systems is a subject that has received very great attention in Britain, and one on which much pioneering work has been done. It may be remembered that the forerunner of the many present-day protective systems of the so-called differential kind is the Merz-Price system, which was developed and first installed on the Newcastle Electric Supply Company’s system near Newcastle-on-Tyne in 1905. Other notable achievements are the first system of carrier-current protection, which was installed in the British grid system in 1931, and, more recently, import- ant advances in the art of busbar-zone protection.

articleTitle: The amplidyne generator—its performance and design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper commences with a brief discussion on the desirability for high amplification and a low time-constant in control apparatus. Then the cross-field principle of operation of the amplidyne, its steady-state operation on D.C. and the effect of varying the compensation of the output stage are briefly analyzed. Both the transient response and the response to a.c. signals of the perfectly compensated machine are treated, as is the a.c. response of the imperfectly compensated generator. The effects of rocking the brushes and of chording the armature windings are briefly noted. Two types of stator construction are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Presidential address
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Two of the most important steps taken by man in his ascendancy over the other creatures of the earth were, first, the devising of implements to assist him in his daily tasks, and, second, the use of some form of power to perform certain of those tasks for him. The latter step probably originated with the domestication of wild animals, followed by the harnessing of simple and obvious natural sources of power such as wind and falling water.

articleTitle: Amplification of pulses by the gating methods
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The shortcomings of conventional pulse amplifiers for radar with respect to ringing, shortest pulse still amplified and signal-to-noise ratio are investigated. Integrating methods using the gating technique are shown to eliminate ringing, make the amplification of shorter pulses possible and improve the signal-to-noise ratio. The improvement in signal-to-noise ratio is achieved at the expense of the speed with which information can be received. The amplification of d.c. pulses is investigated by the simple gate, the double gate and the phase-modulated gate. All three methods eliminate ringing and enable the amplification of shorter pulses. With respect to noise reduction, the simple gate is shown to be inferior to the other two methods due to flicker noise of valves at low frequencies. Neglecting flicker noise, the improvement in signal power to noise power ratio, by using any of the three methods, is equal to the ratio of pulse recurrence frequency to the bandwidth of the amplifier following the gate. An experimental double-gate amplifier is described. The measured signal-to-noise ratio was slightly below the theoretical value, but an improvement of 31 db was nevertheless achieved by gating. The application of the gating technique to a.c. pulses is considered and methods to produce the necessary a.c. pulses locked to the leading edges of d.c. modulating pulses are described.

articleTitle: Specifications and tenders — A symposium
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Intelligent buying of service is clearly the acceptance of the cheapest offer, but to choose the cheapest calls for the nicest judgment on the part of the tenderer in the selection from the number of alternatives he may have available, and that of the purchaser in selecting from the total number of proposals received. ‘Cheap’ is used not colloquially but in the strict sense of ‘worth more than it costs’ which is the only warrant for purchase.

articleTitle: Nuclear energy
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: When I was last privileged to address the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers, on the occasion of the Thirteenth Annual Joint Meeting with the University of the Witwatersrand, in June, 1943, I chose to discuss some engineering aspects of nuclear physics. In the course of that address I referred briefly to the possibility of using the fission of uranium nuclei as a source of power, and pointed out that ‘so far the problem of controlling the undoubted power available in this form of matter has not been solved.’

articleTitle: The characteristics and applications of metal rectifiers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Important developments in physical and electrical research, coupled with improvements in manufacturing technique have, during the recent war, considerably improved the characteristics and greatly extended the field of application of metal rectifiers. Of the many types of ‘dry plate’ or ‘barrier layer’ rectifiers developed, the copper oxide and selenium types are by far the most well-known, mainly by reason of the fact that they have proved by far the most successful. The paper is confined mainly to a brief consideration of the characteristics and a more detailed treatment of the applications of the modern selenium-compound rectifier, which has superseded its copper oxide equivalent for industrial and power applications. It is emphasized, however, that the copper oxide rectifier is not by any means obsolete, in that it possesses characteristics which cause it to be selected for use in certain circuits in preference to the selenium type. For this reason, and also in view of the interest shown by engineers in the relative merits of the two types, some space has been devoted to a comparison of characteristics. The uses of the selenium-compound rectifier are now so numerous and diverse that full treatment in a technical paper is not possible. An effort has therefore been made to summarise a large number of typical applications in concise form and in this process much detail has been omitted. The paper concludes with an indication of the lines along which research and development are now proceeding in an effort to further extend the application of the modern barrier-layer rectifier.

articleTitle: Developments in A. C. winding practice
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: During the last few years there has been a tendency, both in the Transvaal and in the Orange Free State, to install a greater proportion of three-phase a.c. winders as compared to the Ward-Leonard types and some of the reasons for this change are given; these include improvements in dynamic braking and the use of twin a.c. motors of large b.h.p. outputs. This paper reviews the theory of uncompensated and compensated d.c. dyanmic braking, the question of load sharing of twin motors and describes some changes and refinements in rotor control gear specifications which concern primarily a.c. winders.

articleTitle: Electro-mechanical and electronic calculating devices
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper has been prepared for the purpose of examining the progress made in the design of automatic calculators and of investigating the limiting factors in the applications of such equipment to the solution of scientific and mathematical problems. It is felt that a useful purpose will be served in making the general principles of mechanically assisted calculation more widely known, and the author examines the most modern of this equipment (the so-called ‘electronic brain’) and comments on the possible advantages of the construction of a modified version of such a calculator for operation in South Africa. The opinions expressed are those of the author and do not of necessity represent those of the Company with which he is associated.
